title: ULTRA Godot MCP - The fastest Godot MCP server out there!
author: Lordddddddy
selftext: MCP server for Godot Engine that allows AIs and assistants to control projects directly: create scenes, manipulate nodes, manage resources, and validate code, all without opening the editor. While other MCPs launch godot --headless --script per operation (2-5s overhead, usually crashing the editor). Ultra Godot MCP reads and writes .tscn directly with its native parser in milliseconds through an organized session method for the AI Agent.

comments.author: HopefulMeasurement25
comments.body: How does this compare to GodotIQ? I been using it and it is great at doing 3D - so I would like to ask, what does this offer that would make me want to switch?

replies.author: Lordddddddy
replies.body:
Just like GoPeak, GodotIQ has screenshot and visual knowledge, which is really good and a limitation of mine. Advantage of mine is speed, it is really, really fast from my testings and theoretically can be improved a lot. I may add some day visual knowledge, but for now it's sufficient, and I don't think leaving the visual part to the AI is the best idea overall. 

If you just value simplicity, speed and effectiveness, this is your MCP. If you want something controls your workflow COMPLETELY it may not be it. It's just a preference matter

comments.author: TheMisterPirate
comments.body: I've been trying GoPeak MCP, and I have had a few editor crashes, more than a few actually, depending on which LLM I was using. I'll give this a try to see if it avoids that, but I'm curious: you said your approach is to edit the scene files directly. Well, can't coding LLMs already do that? What is this doing differently?

replies.author: Lordddddddy
replies.body:
Those GoPeak crashes are actually pretty common (And the reason I decided to do this) because it relies on launching Godot headless or communicating with the editor via plugins, which are notoriously fragile when an LLM sends an unexpected or malformed command. As for editing .tscn files directly, yes, an LLM could try to do it, but the TSCN format is incredibly strict, it depends on exact load\_steps, auto-incrementing resource IDs, and precise parent-child paths, so one tiny hallucination instantly corrupts the entire scene (Which will later consume tons of tokens fixing it). What makes Ultra Godot MCP different is that it acts as a structured, validated bridge between the AI and the file: you just describe what you want in plain English, and our native Python parser safely handles all the complex syntax, automatically manages ExtResource and SubResource references, and runs a Poka-Yoke validation (Error proof) before writing anything to disk. You get the speed and reliability of direct file editing without the risk of broken scenes or engine crashes, perfect for maximum efficiency, but bad if you just wanna automatize the entirety of the project. 

This is still a bit W.I.P, so there may be errors, but my stress tests showed no errors

comments.author: AnimeDiff
comments.body:
How does it compare to godot mcp pro?

How many tools does this have? 

One thing I see the agents do while making changes is running the scenes and taking screenshots to visually verify information/layout. It can still do this with the editor closed?

replies.author: Lordddddddy
replies.body: It's a very similar architecture to GoPeak in which it makes a websocket to the editor in order to control it. Theoretically it can be heavily optimized through my session method, but I doubt they do sessions, so speed should be noticeably slower. Apart from that, it has more features because it has direct contact with the Editor. This MCP uses a tscn parser and is focused in scene/script creation for maximum efficiency
